questions.q: What do you choose when you set up a provisioned Redshift cluster that you never choose with Redshift Serverless?
options: An AWS Region
A query language
A VPC
A node type and node count
questions.explain: Provisioned clusters require picking a node type (RA3 or DC2) and how many nodes; Serverless allocates RPUs automatically instead.

options: A type of provisioned compute node
The unit S3 uses for storage capacity
A billing unit unique to RA3 nodes
Redshift Processing Unit — the compute/memory unit Redshift Serverless bills by
questions.explain: RPUs are Serverless's capacity unit; the service auto-scales how many are allocated based on query demand.

questions.q: What's the difference between an elastic resize and a classic resize on a provisioned cluster?
options: Elastic resize only works on Redshift Serverless
Elastic resize changes node count within the same node type in minutes; classic resize can change node type and takes longer
They are two names for the exact same operation
Classic resize deletes all table data first
questions.explain: Elastic resize is a fast, same-node-type capacity change with a brief read-only window; classic resize provisions a new cluster (including for a node type change) and cuts over, which takes longer.

questions.q: A team's Redshift query volume spikes hard for three days each quarter and is nearly silent otherwise. What does this lesson suggest for them?
options: A provisioned cluster sized for the quiet days only
A large provisioned cluster sized for the quarterly peak, kept running year-round
No Redshift at all — Athena is required for bursty workloads
Redshift Serverless, since RPUs scale up for the spike and back down during quiet periods
questions.explain: Bursty, unpredictable workloads are the case this lesson gives for Serverless — you avoid paying for peak capacity during the quiet stretches.

questions.q: Why does a provisioned cluster keep costing money even when nobody is running queries?
options: Provisioned clusters cannot be idle by design
You pay for the provisioned node capacity by the hour, regardless of query load
Idle clusters are billed at the same rate as Serverless RPUs
AWS automatically runs background queries to keep the cluster warm
questions.explain: A provisioned cluster's nodes are reserved capacity — you're billed for them being provisioned, not for actual query activity.
